definitions.gloss: considerably, to a great extent, very much
definitions.explanation: Indicates that something is to a much greater degree than expected or normal.

definitions.gloss: almost, nearly, on the verge of
definitions.explanation: Indicates that one nearly did something or was very close to a certain action or state.

examples.japanese: {余程|よほど}{疲|つか}れていたらしい。
examples.english: It seems they were considerably tired.

examples.japanese: {余程|よほど}のことがない{限|かぎ}り{休|やす}まない。
examples.english: I don't take time off unless something really serious happens.

examples.japanese: あの{人|ひと}は{余程|よほど}{自信|じしん}があるのだろう。
examples.english: That person must have a great deal of confidence.

examples.japanese: {余程|よほど}{断|ことわ}ろうかと{思|おも}った。
{余程|よほど}{帰|かえ}ろうかと{思|おも}ったが、{最後|さいご}まで{残|のこ}った。
examples.english: I almost went home, but I stayed until the end.

examples.japanese: あまりにも{失礼|しつれい}で、{余程|よほど}{怒|おこ}ろうかと{思|おも}ったが{我慢|がまん}した。
examples.english: It was so rude that I nearly got angry, but I held back.

notes:
WRITING:
Also written as よほど or よっぽど (casual variant). The kanji {余程|よほど} is used in formal writing.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{余程|よほど}のこと (something extraordinary)
・{余程|よほど}のことがない{限|かぎ}り (unless something extraordinary happens)
・{余程|よほど}〜ようかと{思|おも}った (nearly did ~)

VARIANT:
よっぽど is a more casual spoken form with the same meaning. よほど is slightly more formal.
